reference_use.conclusion: Pinned revisions confirmed and the frozen contract is byte-identical to the snapshot (Submission = Contract), so the nine v1 interfaces remain valid. None of the nine bare names collides with a DAG reservation or with a declaration in the project or SimonGMT sources. All nine statements pass validate_lean_statement and elaborate in the exact comparator NodeChallenge scope. The parent assembly re-derives DeformationTheorem from onto_skeleton, skeleton_polyhedral, im_combination and dilation plus SlicingTheorem and LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity, with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. No Matrix/IsUnit construction occurs. The pinned Mathlib has no multi-dimensional BV Poincaré inequality or BV cut-off/extension lemma (only one-dimensional BoundedVariationOn and the compact-support Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev inequality), so (T4) of deformation_skeleton_polyhedral is proved from Simon Ch. 2, 2.7–2.9 and [GT01, (7.45)]. Simon's printed 2.7 requires δ ∈ (0,1), and his proof of 2.8 needs the inner ball at positive distance from ∂U. The corrected parameters R = √n/2, δ = 1/(2√n) (δR = 1/4, distance 1/4) meet both requirements for every n ≥ 1, as the revised (T4) verifies explicitly.

proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, §5, printed “Proof of the Deformation Theorem”, displays (1)–(7) (pp. 163–164), as reproduced in steps C1–C2 of the parent proof, with the measures M(T⌞·) and M(∂T⌞·) replaced by two arbitrary finite Borel measures μ₁, μ₂ (in the deformation argument they are the mass measures μ_T, μ_∂T, for which M(T⌞A) = μ_T(A)). Errata applied: book k = ℓ; (vi) the printed measure estimate (5) is replaced by the Fubini bound of Step 4 (the printed constants are not needed).

Notation. n := m + 1, d := n + ℓ, ℝ^d = Eucl(m+1+ℓ), C := [0,1]^d, q := (1/2,…,1/2), ω_k := L^k(B_1(0)) for k ≥ 1 and ω₀ := 1. For J ⊆ {1,…,d} with |J| = n + 1 = m + 2 (there are N := C(d, n+1) ≥ 1 such J because ℓ ≥ 1) let S_J := span{e_i : i ∈ J}, p_J : ℝ^d → S_J the orthogonal projection (keep the coordinates in J), x_J := p_J(q), and let B_r(g) denote open balls in S_J (dimension n + 1). For a with |a − q| < 1/4 (equivalently Σ_i(a_i − 1/2)² < 1/16) put L(a) := {y : ∃ J, |J| = n + 1, y_i − a_i ∈ ℤ ∀ i ∈ J} (the set La of the statement).

1. Description of the tubes (printed (2) and the display after (5)). For fixed J let E_J(a) := {y : y_i − a_i ∈ ℤ ∀ i ∈ J} = p_J⁻¹(p_J(a) + ℤ^d ∩ S_J). As E_J(a) is the product of the discrete set p_J(a) + ℤ^d ∩ S_J ⊆ S_J with the complementary coordinate space, dist(x, E_J(a)) = dist(p_J(x), p_J(a) + ℤ^d ∩ S_J). Since L(a) = ⋃_J E_J(a) is a finite union, dist(x, L(a)) = min_J dist(x, E_J(a)). Hence, for σ > 0, with V_J(g, σ) := ⋃_{z ∈ ℤ^d ∩ S_J} p_J⁻¹(B_σ(g + z)) (g ∈ S_J, an open set),
 (1.1) {x : dist(x, L(a)) < σ} = ⋃_J V_J(p_J(a), σ).

2. Good and bad sets (printed (1)). Fix a finite Borel measure μ on ℝ^d and β > 0 (β is fixed in Step 5 and depends only on n, ℓ). For each J let
 G_J := {g ∈ S_J ∩ B_{1/4}(x_J) : μ(V_J(g,σ)) ≤ βσ^{n+1}μ(ℝ^d) for all σ ∈ (0,1/4)}, B_J := (S_J ∩ B_{1/4}(x_J)) ∖ G_J.
 If μ(ℝ^d) = 0 then B_J = ∅. B_J is relatively open in S_J ∩ B_{1/4}(x_J), hence Borel: if b ∈ B_J and σ_b ∈ (0,1/4) satisfies μ(V_J(b,σ_b)) > βσ_b^{n+1}μ(ℝ^d), then for b′ → b, liminf 1_{V_J(b′,σ_b)} ≥ 1_{V_J(b,σ_b)} pointwise (V_J(b′,σ_b) is the translate of the open set V_J(b,σ_b) by b′ − b), so by Fatou's lemma liminf_{b′→b} μ(V_J(b′,σ_b)) ≥ μ(V_J(b,σ_b)) and the strict inequality persists near b.

3. Size of the bad set (printed (2)–(4)). For b ∈ B_J choose σ_b ∈ (0,1/4) with μ(V_J(b,σ_b)) > βσ_b^{n+1}μ(ℝ^d). By the 5-times covering lemma (Simon Ch. 1, 3.4) applied in S_J to the closed balls B̄_{σ_b}(b), b ∈ B_J (diameters ≤ 1/2), there is a pairwise disjoint subfamily {B̄_{σ_i}(b_i)}_{i∈I} — countable, S_J being separable — with B_J ⊆ ⋃_{i∈I} B̄_{5σ_i}(b_i). The open sets p_J⁻¹(B_{σ_i}(b_i + z)), i ∈ I, z ∈ ℤ^d ∩ S_J, are pairwise disjoint: B_{σ_i}(b_i + z) ⊆ B_{1/2}(x_J + z) because |b_i − x_J| < 1/4 and σ_i < 1/4, the balls B_{1/2}(x_J + z), z ∈ ℤ^d ∩ S_J, are pairwise disjoint (their centres are at mutual distance ≥ 1), and for equal z the balls B_{σ_i}(b_i + z) are disjoint by the choice of the subfamily. Therefore, if I ≠ ∅ (which forces μ(ℝ^d) > 0),
 β Σ_{i∈I} σ_i^{n+1} μ(ℝ^d) < Σ_{i∈I} μ(V_J(b_i,σ_i)) ≤ μ(ℝ^d), so Σ_i σ_i^{n+1} ≤ β⁻¹,
 and L^{n+1}(B_J) ≤ Σ_i ω_{n+1}(5σ_i)^{n+1} ≤ 5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}β⁻¹ (also true if I = ∅, i.e. B_J = ∅).

4. Fubini (corrected (5)). Let A_J := {a ∈ B_{1/4}(q) : p_J(a) ∈ B_J}, a Borel set (note p_J(a) ∈ S_J ∩ B_{1/4}(x_J) for every a ∈ B_{1/4}(q)). Write ℝ^d = S_J × S_J^⊥, where S_J^⊥ is spanned by the ℓ − 1 coordinates outside J. For b ∈ S_J the fibre {w ∈ S_J^⊥ : b + w ∈ B_{1/4}(q)} is contained in the (ℓ−1)-dimensional ball of radius 1/4 centred at q − x_J, of measure ω_{ℓ−1}4^{−(ℓ−1)} (a point when ℓ = 1). By Fubini–Tonelli,
 L^d(A_J) ≤ L^{n+1}(B_J)·ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ} ≤ 5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ}β⁻¹.

5. Choice of β and of a (printed (6), (7)). Choose β = β(n,ℓ) > 0 so large that 2N·5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ}β⁻¹ < ω_d4^{−d} = L^d(B_{1/4}(q)). Apply Steps 2–4 with this β to μ := μ₁ and to μ := μ₂, obtaining sets G_J^{(1)}, A_J^{(1)} and G_J^{(2)}, A_J^{(2)}. Then L^d(⋃_J (A_J^{(1)} ∪ A_J^{(2)})) ≤ 2N·5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ}β⁻¹ < L^d(B_{1/4}(q)), so there is a ∈ B_{1/4}(q) belonging to no A_J^{(i)}; i.e. Σ_i(a_i − 1/2)² < 1/16 and p_J(a) ∈ G_J^{(1)} ∩ G_J^{(2)} for every J. Let La = L(a). For σ ∈ (0, 1/4) and i ∈ {1,2}, by (1.1) and the definition of G_J^{(i)}:
 μ_i({x : dist(x, La) < σ}) ≤ Σ_J μ_i(V_J(p_J(a), σ)) ≤ Nβσ^{n+1}μ_i(ℝ^d) = Nβσ^{m+2}μ_i(univ).

6. Conclusion. c := Nβ ∈ [0,∞) depends only on (m, ℓ), and the point a of Step 5 has all required properties, for any finite Borel measures μ₁, μ₂. ∎
key_steps: Good/bad sets G_J, B_J in S_J ∩ B_{1/4}(x_J) for a fixed finite measure μ and β; B_J relatively open.
5-times covering and disjointness of the periodic tubes: L^{n+1}(B_J) ≤ 5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}β⁻¹ (printed (2)–(4)).
Choose β so that the bad sets for μ₁ and μ₂ together miss part of B_{1/4}(q); pick a there; sum over J: μ_i({d_a < σ}) ≤ Nβσ^{n+1}μ_i(ℝ^d) (printed (6),(7)).
